summary: The [National Digital Transformation Agenda 2022-2025](2023-11-27 Setting the agenda for digital transformation) has run out its period, and no successor agenda is held.
developments:
The agenda set four axes and its period has since ended, with no successor, evaluation or extension on record ([agenda](2023-11-27 Setting the agenda for digital transformation)).

The pattern repeats across this unit: the cybersecurity strategy and the university research accreditation both expired in the same way, so what the base records is a set of instruments that ran their term and were not replaced.

summary: A [National AI Strategy 2025-2029](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) is recorded as existing by a reference guide, and its text is not held.
developments:
The strategy is recorded as existing and nothing establishes its scope, commitments, budget or implementing body ([strategy](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

No draft, adoption instrument, workshop or consultation for it appears anywhere else in the base, so the country's artificial-intelligence position is a title in somebody else's directory.

summary: The [data protection law](2017-07-22-mauritania-loi-2017-020-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel) has been in force since July 2017, requiring approved codes of conduct and free, unambiguous consent, with no enforcement decision published.
developments:
The statute covers both manual and electronic processing and requires codes of conduct approved by the authority and free, unambiguous consent ([law](2017-07-22-mauritania-loi-2017-020-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel)).

The authority runs monthly ordinary meetings and sensitisation days for ministries, telecom operators and financial institutions, and no enforcement decision, register entry, sanction or annual report is published ([authority](2026-05-06-mauritania-apd-site-institutionnel)). The held extraction of the law cuts off mid-article, so the chapters covering the authority's powers and sanctions are not captured.

summary: The transport regulator gave ride-hailing applications [fifteen days to bring their authorisations into line](2026-08-24-mauritania-ride-hailing-apps-15-day-compliance-deadline) in August 2026, warning of suspension.
developments:
The communique warned that failure within the deadline could bring legal proceedings including suspension of the activity, with no further notice or warning required, and set the warning against growing use of digital platforms for transport services ([communique](2026-08-24-mauritania-ride-hailing-apps-15-day-compliance-deadline)).

No operator is named and no count of non-compliant authorisations is given. It is the base's only record of platform activity being regulated in the country, and it reaches the platforms through transport law rather than through any digital statute.

summary: The [data protection authority](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) is established and operating under a 2023-2026 plan, with no decision, register or annual report held.
developments:
Its existence and plan are recorded by a reference guide ([guide](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

Nine years after the statute, the base holds no decision, no register of declared processing, no enforcement action and no annual report from it, so what can be established is that the institution exists and not that it acts.

summary: A [digital cooperation memorandum with Senegal](2025-01-16-senegal-mauritania-digital-mou) was signed in January 2025, with no deliverable, workstream or funding under it on record.
developments:
The memorandum was signed in January 2025 and nothing has followed it into the base ([memorandum](2025-01-16-senegal-mauritania-digital-mou)).

It is the only bilateral instrument with a neighbour on file. The country's other recorded international digital engagements run to the Gulf and to European financiers rather than along its own borders.

summary: The [1989 Maghreb Union treaty](1989-02-17-uma-treaty-instituting-arab-maghreb-union) is in force with a binding judicial organ and no summit since 1994.
developments:
The [treaty concluded at Marrakesh in February 1989](1989-02-17-uma-treaty-instituting-arab-maghreb-union) has been in force since 1 July 1989 and establishes a presidential council, a council of foreign ministers, a general secretariat, a consultative council and a judicial organ whose rulings bind.

No summit has been held since 1994, so the instrument supplies a legal frame for harmonisation and no working machinery. Harmonisation between Maghreb states therefore proceeds bilaterally where it proceeds at all.

summary: A vendor with two European donors was [named for Sahel digital connectivity support](2026-06-15-ericsson-luxembourg-sweden-sahel-digital-connectivity) in June 2026, with no site, capacity or delivery figure for the country published.
developments:
The announcement names an equipment vendor working with two European government funders on Sahel connectivity ([announcement](2026-06-15-ericsson-luxembourg-sweden-sahel-digital-connectivity)).

No Mauritanian site, capacity or delivery figure is published, so the country appears in a regional programme whose national share cannot be established.

summary: A [public digital service standards framework](2026-03-27-public-digital-services-standards-framework-techafricanews) is under development with German support, and the [state agency proposed to operate interoperability](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables) has never been created.
developments:
A three-day standards and interoperability workshop was run by the ministry in March 2026 with German support; no framework or standard has been published ([workshop](2026-03-27-public-digital-services-standards-framework-techafricanews)).

The agency intended to operate national interoperability was proposed in July 2021 as a public establishment under the digital ministry with about fifty staff, EUR 220,000 to set up and EUR 1.4m a year to run, with a draft creation decree ([proposal](2021-07-31-mauritania-aneta-digital-agency-proposal-undp)). A June 2023 open-data strategy proposed reviving that decree to name the same body national interoperability operator, and no adoption, decree or launch is on record ([strategy](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables)).

summary: [All licensed operators have activated IPv6](2026-07-24-mauritania-all-operators-activate-ipv6-national-strategy), with one past 15 per cent of subscribers migrated against the [strategy](2024-05-01-mauritanie-strategie-nationale-transition-ipv6) target of 25 per cent by the end of 2026.
developments:
A sixty-eight page national transition strategy set a target of 25 per cent adoption by 2026 with a national transition committee ([strategy](2024-05-01-mauritanie-strategie-nationale-transition-ipv6)); it carries no printed adoption date and its economic-impact figures are lifted from a consultancy report rather than measured ([strategy](2024-05-01-mauritanie-strategie-nationale-transition-ipv6)).

By July 2026 all licensed operators had activated IPv6 across networks and services, with one unnamed operator past 15 per cent of subscribers migrated ([activation](2026-07-24-mauritania-all-operators-activate-ipv6-national-strategy)). The target is the clearest measurable commitment the country has made on a technical standard, and it is on course to be missed.

progress: Mixed, the ministry's budget more than doubling while the universal access fund's governing decree was repealed as unclear
summary: The digital ministry's budget reached [US$24.2m for 2026, up 104.6 per cent](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin), while the [universal access fund decree](2026-07-29-lequotidien-conseil-ministres-fonds-acces-universel) was repealed for unclear object and resource allocation.
developments:
The ministry's 2026 budget is US$24.2m, up 104.6 per cent on the previous year ([budget](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin)).

The Council of Ministers approved a decree in July 2026 repealing the fund's 2020 governing decree, on grounds that the fund's object, its resource mobilisation and allocation, and its integration into the state budgetary system were all unclear; the new terms are not published and neither decree is held ([repeal](2026-07-29-lequotidien-conseil-ministres-fonds-acces-universel)).

So the domestic money for digital transformation grew sharply in the same year the instrument for spending it on universal access was found not to work.

summary: A [regional digital programme](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin) financed the national cloud, a [US$30m reform grant](2021-07-22-wb-mrt-001-mauritania-2nd-second-private-sector-digital) was disbursed, and [US$50m more](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech) was agreed in principle in April 2026.
developments:
The regional digital programme financed the national cloud launched in June 2026, and its national public key infrastructure procurement remains unawarded ([programme](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin), [appraisal](2023-11-07-worldbank-dtfa-wardip-sop1-pad4756)).

A US$30m grant was disbursed in 2021 as the second of three planned private sector, digital and human capital reform operations, and no third operation is on record ([grant](2021-07-22-wb-mrt-001-mauritania-2nd-second-private-sector-digital), [operation](2021-06-22 Mauritania Second Private Sector, Digital and Human Capital Reform DPF (P171238, World Bank))).

An agreement in principle for US$50m covering digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, interoperability and skills was reached in April 2026 ([agreement](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech)); no signed instrument, disbursement or schedule is held ([agreement](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech), [record](2026-01-01-islamic-development-bank-mrt-2026-mauritania-digital-transformation-bw11)).

summary: [Four fifteen-year 5G licences](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews) were awarded in 2026 and the first commercial network launched at Nouakchott in August, with no coverage or subscriber figure published.
developments:
Licences went to the three incumbents and a new entrant at bids of MRU 252.6m to 305m plus 5 per cent of revenue, breaking the three-operator structure ([licences](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews)).

One operator launched the country's first commercial 5G network at Nouakchott on 10 August 2026 under the digital transformation minister; no coverage footprint, tariff or subscriber figure is published ([launch](2026-08-11-mauritania-chinguitel-5g-launch), [account](2026-08-10-mauritania-chinguitel-5g-launch)).

The same operator had completed a full network modernisation at Nouakchott with a foreign vendor in November 2025, again with no coverage, capacity or subscriber figure published ([modernisation](2025-11-13-chinguitel-huawei-network-modernisation-techafricanews)).

summary: The [one international cable since 2011](2026-05-05-second-cable-connectivity-baseline-ecofin) is to be joined by a [second](2026-05-04-ellalink-second-cable-phase1-landing-ami) commissioning in early 2027, with a [third financed and unlanded](2022-01-01-eib-mrt-002-medusa-submarine-cable-system-ssa-component).
developments:
A single submarine cable has been the country's only international connection since 2011 ([cable](2026-05-05-second-cable-connectivity-baseline-ecofin), [baseline](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB))).

The second cable was launched at Nouadhibou in July 2025 at 669 km and 200 Gb/s rising to 12 Tbit/s, European-financed; phase-one coastal landing is complete, offshore laying was scheduled for August 2026 and commissioning is expected in the first quarter of 2027 ([landing](2026-05-04-ellalink-second-cable-phase1-landing-ami), [launch](2025-07-28-ellalink-second-cable-launch-ami)).

A third system's sub-Saharan component is financed with no landing, route or commissioning date on record ([financing](2022-01-01-eib-mrt-002-medusa-submarine-cable-system-ssa-component)). A country dependent on one cable for fifteen years is the position the other two are meant to end.

summary: [Three firms were provisionally selected](2026-07-07-mauritanie-trois-entreprises-selectionnees-services-telecoms-satellite) for satellite internet licences across two lots in July 2026, with no award or operating framework published.
developments:
The tender opened in January 2026 and nine bids were received, from which three firms were provisionally retained, two of them required to match the leading offer ([selection](2026-07-07-mauritanie-trois-entreprises-selectionnees-services-telecoms-satellite), [tender](2026-01-29-satellite-internet-licence-tender-are-techafricanews)).

Thirteen firms took the dossier, and the leading bid was US$800,000 for the mobile lot and US$3m for capacity against US$50,000 and MRU 6.5m from the other two ([bids](2026-07-07-mauritanie-trois-entreprises-selectionnees-services-telecoms-satellite)).

The regulator's own communique is not held and the figures reach the base through a trade account of it. No award, launch date or operating framework has been published.

summary: A [EUR 15m Tier III national data centre](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB)) has been in service since May 2025, and a [national cloud](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin) launched on it in June 2026.
developments:
The data centre was inaugurated on 8 May 2025, European-financed at EUR 15m and certified, operated by the international telecoms company ([data centre](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB))); no capacity, utilisation or migration figure has been published since ([data centre](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB)), [construction](2025-08-20 Construction of a Datacenter in Nouakchott, Mauritania (EEAS))).

The national cloud launched in June 2026 to host government data and services domestically and centralise public information technology, with no migration timeline, capacity or cost disclosed; as at August 2026 it was in data-security testing and migration preparation ahead of go-live ([launch](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin), [testing](2026-08-11-mauritania-world-bank-national-data-centre-visit)).

summary: The electricity utility's [2024 procurement plan](2024-12-04-mauritania-somelec-pppm-2024-procurement-plan) itemises a data-centre fit-out, an enterprise system and smart-metering and dispatch studies, none reported complete.
developments:
The plan itemises a donor-financed data-centre fit-out launched in July 2023 and due October 2024, an enterprise resource planning and customer relationship system in procurement due June 2025, a second planning study due December 2025, a geo-referenced database for the national electrification strategy due October 2025, and advanced-metering and national-dispatch studies due late 2025; two telecoms engineers were recruited under a development bank's financing ([plan](2024-12-04-mauritania-somelec-pppm-2024-procurement-plan)).

No item is reported complete. The utility's own data centre is distinct from the government's national facility, so the state runs two data-centre programmes and has published an outturn for neither.

summary: A [390-post civil service competition](2026-08-19-lequotidien-concours-recrutement-390-agents-numerise) was run digitally from application to examination in August 2026, inside a [3,000-post recruitment programme](2026-08-18-ami-mauritanie-concours-recrutement-390-numerise).
developments:
Applications were filed through the state services platform and examinations sat on digital tablets at Nouakchott, for a 390-post competition inside a wider programme for 3,000 state employees and contract workers ([competition](2026-08-19-lequotidien-concours-recrutement-390-agents-numerise), [examination](2026-08-18-ami-mauritanie-concours-recrutement-390-numerise)).

It is the first competition the base holds that is digital end to end rather than at the application stage only. No candidate count, marking method, accessibility provision or fallback for a candidate unable to use a tablet is published, and nothing states how the results are audited.

progress: Mixed, the national strategy expired with its planned response team never built while a central-bank platform detected threats at scale
summary: The [cybersecurity strategy](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) ran out in 2025 with no successor and the [response team it provided for](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) was never built, while a [central-bank platform](2026-07-08-pafiid-bcm-cyber-threats-elvetach) detected more than 10,000 threats.
developments:
The 2022-2025 strategy's period has ended and no successor, evaluation or response team is on record; the strategy text itself is not held ([strategy](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

The national computer emergency response team is planned, with no establishing instrument, staffing or premises on record ([team](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

A central bank digital reputation protection platform detected more than 10,000 electronic threats in the first half of 2026, of which 470 were confirmed and removed, with 20 digital identities protected ([platform](2026-07-08-pafiid-bcm-cyber-threats-elvetach)). The country's only operating detection capability sits inside one institution and covers that institution's own exposure.

summary: A [national data management system](2026-07-29-mauritania-blockchain-public-services-undp) is being scoped for inter-administration integration, with blockchain proposed as its trust layer.
developments:
A two-day workshop on data governance and blockchain in public administration opened on 27 July 2026 ([workshop](2026-07-27-ami-atelier-blockchain-administration-publique)).

The system is being scoped on a national blockchain policy in consultation since November 2025, naming land administration, trade, public procurement and natural-resource management as its first domains; no draft text, adoption date or budget is published ([scoping](2026-07-29-mauritania-blockchain-public-services-undp)). The interoperability operator that would run such a system has been proposed twice and never created.

progress: Mixed, about 1.5 million users and half a million remote services against a full day of scheduled maintenance taking every dependent service down at once
summary: The [national identity application](2026-06-21-houwiyeti-usage-metrics-techrek) serves about 1.5 million citizens and 554,027 remote services, and a [full day of maintenance](2026-08-11-mauritania-houwiyeti-outage-digital-sovereignty) on 8 August 2026 took all of it down together.
developments:
The application launched in 2024 on a vendor identity platform carrying document extracts and passport requests ([launch](2024-08-15 Mauritania Launches Digital ID for e-Services, Built on TECH5 Platform (Houwiyeti)), [pilot](2024-08-01 Mauritania pilots digital ID app (e-ID Mauritania))).

It is in use by about 1.5 million citizens for 554,027 remote services and is the identity-verification backbone for the state services portal's fifteen-plus services and for private financial applications ([usage](2026-06-21-houwiyeti-usage-metrics-techrek), [account](2024-08-02 Mauritania launches digital ID app to boost access to services and improve governance)).

A full day of scheduled maintenance on 8 August 2026 took all of it down at once; no operator statement on the outage or on redundancy is held ([outage](2026-08-11-mauritania-houwiyeti-outage-digital-sovereignty)). A single point of failure carrying that many dependent services is the finding here, and the base holds no continuity arrangement for it.

summary: The [population register](2026-06-18-etat-civil-parliamentary-id-exclusion-ladepeche) reached 5.1m entries against 3.4m in 2019, with enrolment now a permanent public service, and a contested residual without papers.
developments:
Figures given to deputies in June 2026 put 5.1m on the register against 3.4m in 2019, with more than 1.7m new enrolments, over 613,000 people captured by a difficulties survey and 238 local commissions installed ([register](2026-06-18-etat-civil-parliamentary-id-exclusion-ladepeche)); enrolment is now a permanent public service under the 2025 reform ([register](2026-06-18-etat-civil-parliamentary-id-exclusion-ladepeche)).

More than 94 per cent of the population had been reported enrolled since 2020 ([coverage](2025-05-20 African nations making digital ID gains in the face of common challenges (ID4Africa 2025))). A contested residual of citizens without papers falls disproportionately on two population groups and sits in tension with the aggregate coverage claim, which is why the difficulties survey exists.

summary: The transport minister stated in August 2026 that [driving licences and registration plates](2026-08-21-ami-mauritanie-numerisation-permis-conduire-plaques) would be issued in biometric form before the end of 2026.
developments:
The statement came alongside continued reform of the land transport directorate ([statement](2026-08-21-ami-mauritanie-numerisation-permis-conduire-plaques)).

It is a stated target with no procurement, supplier or system specification published, and it is the only credential besides the national identity card and the passport that the country has committed to issuing biometrically.

summary: A [national public key infrastructure and certificate management system](2026-06-10-wardip-mauritanie-additif-n2-ap01-identite-numerique-pki) went to tender in two lots under donor credit and was twice extended, with no award held.
developments:
A second addendum of 10 June 2026 moved the proposal deadline and the public opening to 21 July 2026 and proposal validity to 22 November 2026, on IDA credit 7445-MR ([addendum](2026-06-10-wardip-mauritanie-additif-n2-ap01-identite-numerique-pki)); the earlier notice had put evaluation at 40 per cent technical and 60 per cent cost ([tender](2026-04-28-wardip-mauritanie-ap01-identite-numerique-pki)).

The notice title promises a national digital identity system but the operative text describes only electronic certification integrating with the existing register, so what is being procured is narrower than what it is called. No award is held.

summary: [Formal notices](2026-01-16 Mauritania Steps Up Pressure on Telecom Operators Over Biometric Identification) went to all three operators in January 2026 over biometric SIM identification, with a two-month deadline before sanctions of up to 3 per cent of turnover.
developments:
Deactivation of non-biometric cards had been ordered in October 2023 with compliance not established; formal notices with a two-month deadline followed in January 2026 ([notices](2026-01-16 Mauritania Steps Up Pressure on Telecom Operators Over Biometric Identification)).

No compliance outcome is on record. Three years between an order and a sanction threat, with no published measure of how many cards were affected either time, is the shape of enforcement here.

summary: A [tax on electronic transactions](2026-01-17-loi-finances-2026-electronic-transaction-tax-investtime) took effect in 2026, the [electronic tax platform](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop) has 66 public bodies enrolled, and [electronic invoicing](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop) was announced.
developments:
The 2026 finance law levies 0.1 per cent on electronic transactions above MRU 5,000 and 10 per cent on agent commissions, collected at source ([tax](2026-01-17-loi-finances-2026-electronic-transaction-tax-investtime)).

The electronic tax services platform has 66 public bodies enrolled, 53 filing electronically and 3 paying through it, against 642 legally constituted public bodies of which 339 are active with the tax administration; more than 500 taxpayers overall are on the platform, producing 36.45 per cent of directorate revenue in 2026 ([platform](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop)).

Electronic invoicing for public institutions was announced in July 2026 to handle value-added tax and withholding at source by transferring data automatically to the tax directorate, with no instrument, supplier or date published ([invoicing](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop)).

summary: Financial inclusion is put at [55 per cent in 2026 against 21 per cent in 2019-20](2026-04-13-pamif-financial-inclusion-afdb) on the financier's own account, with one bank's transfers rising from 5,000 a year to 94,000 in a half-year.
developments:
Telecompensation, real-time settlement and automated refinancing were reported delivered under a US$4.78m modernisation project, with inclusion at 55 per cent in 2026 against 21 per cent in 2019-20 and one bank's transfers rising from 5,000 in the whole of 2023 to 94,000 in the second half of 2025 ([project](2026-04-13-pamif-financial-inclusion-afdb)).

The figures are the development bank's account of its own project rather than a central-bank series, and a second phase targets financial technology firms. No account count, wallet figure or agent network measure is independently held.

summary: A [unified digital consular registry](2026-07-29-mauritania-two-consular-digital-platforms-gulf-maldives) went live for three countries in 2026, registering residence, distribution and permitted activities of citizens abroad.
developments:
The registry is live for the Riyadh mission's zone of competence, covering Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and the Maldives, and builds a digital register of national skills abroad ([registry](2026-07-29-mauritania-two-consular-digital-platforms-gulf-maldives), [services](2026-07-10-digital-consular-services-diaspora-wearetech)).

The consular registration desk remains the competent authority, so the platform layers onto the registry rather than replacing it. No enrolment count for the diaspora it covers is published.

summary: A [decree of 27 August 2026](2026-08-27-ami-conseil-ministres-cadastre-numerique-casier-judiciaire) creates a national digital cadastral reference with a unique identifier for every parcel, where no integrated cadastral system existed.
developments:
The government's cadastre digitisation was publicly criticised as a route to silent dispossession in a country where land is at the heart of social conflict ([critique](2026-08-28-kassataya-mauritanie-le-numerique-comme-instrument-de-depossession-silencieuse)). The critique is one outlet's; what the base does not hold is any safeguard, appeal route or consultation record attached to the digitisation.

The Council of Ministers adopted a decree on 27 August 2026 establishing a national digital reference for land and cadastral data as the state's authoritative source, with a permanent, unique, non-duplicable identifier for every parcel independent of administrative divisions, the land minister stating that no integrated cadastral survey system meeting these requirements has existed ([decree](2026-08-27-ami-conseil-ministres-cadastre-numerique-casier-judiciaire)). The decree states expressly that neither the reference nor the cadastral certificate creates or extinguishes any real property right.

summary: An [education certificate service](2025-07-24-houwiyati-national-certificates-service-ami) runs on the national identity application for certificates issued after 2013 or linked to the identity number, with no usage figure held.
developments:
The service extracts and confirms national education certificates through the identity application ([service](2025-07-24-houwiyati-national-certificates-service-ami)).

It covers certificates issued after 2013 or otherwise linked to the national identity number, which puts a date before which the record is not reachable digitally. No usage figure, coverage share or education management information system for the country is held.

summary: An [administrative procedures portal](2026-02-22 Mauritania Centralizes 800 Administrative Procedures in New Digital Portal (Ijraati)) consolidates more than 800 procedures, [consular services](2026-07-10-digital-consular-services-diaspora-wearetech) went online in July 2026, and [water utility transactions](2026-08-04-ami-numerisation-services-snde-portail-mes-services) joined the services portal in August.
developments:
The procedures portal launched in February 2026 as a directory of more than 800 procedures with documents, processing times, agencies and tracking; no usage figure is published ([portal](2026-02-22 Mauritania Centralizes 800 Administrative Procedures in New Digital Portal (Ijraati))).

A consular platform launched on 9 July 2026 with nine online services covering registration, the consular card, travel authorisation, legalisation, powers of attorney, appointments and burial and repatriation permits, built by diaspora engineers with the ministry after consultations in twenty-two countries ([platform](2026-07-10-digital-consular-services-diaspora-wearetech), [services](2026-07-29-mauritania-two-consular-digital-platforms-gulf-maldives)).

The water utility's transactions became available remotely from 4 August 2026 ([utility](2026-08-04-ami-numerisation-services-snde-portail-mes-services)), and a remote transactions platform named in a roadmap is now the subject of integration work with the territorial-administration system, reported as under discussion rather than delivered ([integration](2026-08-13-mauritania-diwan-khidmaty-digitalization-german-cooperation)).

summary: The [mobile market went from three operators to four](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews) at the 5G award in April 2026, the first change in the market structure on record.
developments:
A new entrant was licensed alongside the three incumbents at the provisional 5G award ([award](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews)).

No domestic manufacturing, software production or supplier capability is recorded anywhere in the base, so the country's industrial position in this sector is the number of licensed operators and nothing else.

summary: A [Startup Act](2024-01-02-mauritania-loi-de-startup-ministry-page) was promulgated in January 2024 with a merit-based label, a state-backed fund and procurement preference, and its enacted text is not held.
developments:
The draft that went to consultation targeted 300 labelled start-ups and 3,000 jobs over five years, and set out a merit-based label with a preferential public-procurement margin, a state-backed start-up fund and guarantee fund with investor tax incentives, payroll-cost relief, a technology-innovation hub, and intellectual property and customs relief ([draft](2023-09-07-mauritania-startup-act-presentation-projet-de-loi)).

The law was promulgated on 2 January 2024 ([promulgation](2024-01-02-mauritania-loi-de-startup-ministry-page)). The promulgated text itself is not held, so whether those provisions survived into law cannot be established, and no count of labelled firms, fund disbursements or jobs has been published since.

summary: The national university opened a [first summer school on language models for low-resource African languages](2026-08-25-ami-nouakchott-ai-language-models-summer-school) in August 2026.
developments: The University of Nouakchott opened the first edition of a summer school on language models for low-resource African languages at Nouadhibou on 25 August 2026, taking participants from corpus construction and semantic annotation through model adaptation and evaluation to prototypes in translation and conversational assistants ([summer school](2026-08-25-ami-nouakchott-ai-language-models-summer-school)). No participant count, budget or repeat commitment is stated.

summary: A [youth digital employability programme](2026-07-23-ami-projet-employabilite-jeunes-numerique) launched in July 2026 for 2,150 beneficiaries across six cities, about 2,000 of them young people.
developments:
The programme is financed by a French fund and delivered by an external implementer, succeeding a predecessor that closed in 2025; the implementer puts its three-year record at about 5,000 people given basic digital skills ([programme](2026-07-23-ami-projet-employabilite-jeunes-numerique)).

No completion, certification or placement figure is published for the current programme, and no national count of digital graduates or of employment in the sector is held.

summary: The university's [computing and data sciences research unit](2023-01-05-mauritania-universite-nouakchott-calcul-scientifique-data-sciences) lost its accreditation period in May 2024 with no renewal published, having held sixteen doctoral candidates.
developments:
The unit at the science and technology faculty was accredited for May 2021 to May 2024 and held sixteen doctoral candidates concentrated in artificial intelligence and data science, covering network optimisation, distributed-ledger and internet-of-things process mining, health-data management and cloud-resource elasticity, with three theses defended in 2022 ([unit](2023-01-05-mauritania-universite-nouakchott-calcul-scientifique-data-sciences)).

The accreditation period ended in May 2024 with no renewal published. It is the only research capability on the country's digital questions in the base, and its formal standing lapsed two years ago.

summary: The [fifth population and housing census](2026-08-03-mauritania-census-digitization) was conducted entirely electronically for the first time, with final regional results presented from August 2026.
developments:
Mapping, collection, processing and analysis were all digital, and final results were presented at regional workshops from 3 August 2026 ([census](2026-08-03-mauritania-census-digitization)).

The all-electronic claim is the statistics agency's own and no methodology document is held, so what the base establishes is that the agency says the operation was digital end to end and not how it was done.

summary: A [National Youth Empowerment Index](2026-07-29-lequotidien-indice-national-autonomisation-jeunes) was published in preliminary form at 60.5 out of 100 for 2026, built from 43 secondary indicators across five domains.
developments:
The reference document was presented at a Nouakchott workshop on 29 July 2026, with education and training strongest at 69.5 per cent and health and sport weakest at 46.1 per cent ([index](2026-07-29-lequotidien-indice-national-autonomisation-jeunes)).

It is built from secondary indicators rather than new collection, which makes it a use of administrative and survey data the state already holds. No methodology note, weighting scheme or update cycle is published.

summary: The [national open data portal](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables) carries 24 downloadable datasets from four public providers, last of four benchmarked countries on every published measure.
developments:
The portal is run by the statistics agency and carries 24 datasets from four providers, with no membership of the international open-government partnership ([strategy](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables)).

A June 2023 national open-data strategy proposed a new governance framework, a portal redesign and reviving the decree creating a state digital agency as operator; none of that is reported delivered three years later, and the portal is where it was.

summary: A [Chinese government grant of MUR 629.4m](2021-01-01-china-mofcom-mrt-001-chinese-government-provides-mur-6294-million) funded an urban security system, with no delivery, siting or oversight arrangement on record.
developments:
The grant was recorded in 2021 through a bilateral cooperation agreement ([grant](2021-01-01-china-mofcom-mrt-001-chinese-government-provides-mur-6294-million)).

Five years on, no delivery, siting or oversight arrangement for the system is on record. A surveillance deployment funded by a foreign state with no published oversight is the kind of thing a data-protection authority would be expected to have ruled on, and no decision of the authority is held on anything.

summary: European financiers put [more than EUR 43.5m](2025-01-01-eib-mrt-2025-ellalink-submarine-cable-connection-bw04) into the second submarine cable, funded [resilience work](2020-01-01-eib-mrt-001-mauritania-covid-19-resilience-submarine-cable) in 2020, and run a [EUR 4m German cooperation project](2024-01-01-bmz-mrt-001-promotion-of-digital-transformation-digital-y-forderung).
developments:
More than EUR 43.5m was committed by the European investment bank and the union for the second cable connection, with construction under way and the cable not yet commissioned ([financing](2025-01-01-eib-mrt-2025-ellalink-submarine-cable-connection-bw04), [launch](2025-07-28-ellalink-second-cable-launch-ami)).

A resilience submarine cable financing was committed in 2020 with no completion or outcome report held ([resilience](2020-01-01-eib-mrt-001-mauritania-covid-19-resilience-submarine-cable)).

A German cooperation project has run since January 2025 at EUR 4m, supporting the public digital service standards framework, with no output or completion report published ([project](2024-01-01-bmz-mrt-001-promotion-of-digital-transformation-digital-y-forderung), [framework](2026-03-27-public-digital-services-standards-framework-techafricanews)). European money is the largest single source in the country's digital record, and none of the three carries a published result.

summary: A [cooperation agreement with Oman](2026-07-31-oman-mauritania-sign-5-mous-to-boost-digital-economy-cooperation) was signed in July 2026 across five instruments, and the [Islamic Development Bank](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech) agreed US$50m in principle in April.
developments:
The Omani agreement and accompanying memoranda cover digital capacity-building, electronic training, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and data analytics, platform development and civil-service programmes, signed at the close of a Nouakchott forum with no value disclosed by either side ([agreement](2026-07-31-oman-mauritania-sign-5-mous-to-boost-digital-economy-cooperation), [forum](2026-07-30-lequotidien-forum-mauritanie-oman-numerisation-accords)).

The development bank's agreement in principle covers digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, interoperability and skills, with no signed instrument, disbursement or schedule held ([agreement in principle](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech)).

Between them these are the largest recent commitments to the country's digital programme, and neither has a signed value on record ([delegation](2026-07-29-ami-ministre-transformation-numerique-delegation-omanaise), [business forum](2026-07-30-ami-forum-affaires-mauritanie-oman-numerisation)).

progress: Advanced, the strategy period expired with a successor only in preparation
summary: The [national digital transformation agenda for 2022-2025](2022-06-01-mtnima-agenda-national-transformation-numerique-2022-2025) has run out, and [preparation of a 2030 successor began in December 2025](2025-12-04-ami-lancement-preparation-agenda-national-transformation-numerique-2030).
developments:
The 2022 agenda is now held as the ministry's own document, carrying a vision, objectives, strategic orientations, implementation levers and project sheets ([agenda](2022-06-01-mtnima-agenda-national-transformation-numerique-2022-2025)).

The ministry announced on 4 December 2025 that work on a National Digital Transformation Agenda 2030 had begun ([successor](2025-12-04-ami-lancement-preparation-agenda-national-transformation-numerique-2030)).

No implementation report, budget outturn or project-by-project status against the 2022 agenda's sheets is published, so a four-year strategy closed without the base holding what it delivered.

summary: A [broadband promotion and universal access strategy](2019-02-01-mesrstic-strategie-promotion-haut-debit-acces-universel-volume-1) was completed in February 2019 with an action plan beside it, and no successor or implementation report is held.
developments:
The strategy volume sets quantified coverage and capacity objectives, market segments and an indicative budget, and calls for a National Broadband Plan to be put in place; it proposes regulatory action on the wholesale market, a wholesale catalogue and a tariff structure ([strategy](2019-02-01-mesrstic-strategie-promotion-haut-debit-acces-universel-volume-1), [action plan](2019-01-01-mesrstic-plan-actions-strategie-nationale-promotion-haut-debit-volume-2)).

Seven years on, the base holds no adoption instrument, no implementation report and no successor, and nothing establishes whether the National Broadband Plan it calls for was ever made.

summary: The [cybercrime law of 2016](2016-01-01-mauritanie-loi-2016-007-relative-a-la-cybercriminalite) is the instrument in force, its text now held; no amendment is on the record.
developments:
Law n. 2016-007 defines computer data, subscriber data and traffic data and sets the offences and procedure for cybercrime ([law](2016-01-01-mauritanie-loi-2016-007-relative-a-la-cybercriminalite)).

Against it, a [national emergency response team and security operations centre were put out to international tender in September 2025](2025-09-01-wardip-appel-offres-csirt-national-soc-riad-additif-2) and no award is on the record.

The base holds no prosecution count, case record or amendment, so the statute is dated and its use is not.

summary: The [civil status code of 2011](2011-01-12-mauritanie-qanun-2011-003-mudawwanat-al-hala-al-madaniya-sijil-watani-lilsukkan) created the national population register, and [law 2025-011 replaced certain of its provisions](2025-02-24-mauritanie-loi-2025-011-modifiant-code-etat-civil-actes-numeriques) in February 2025.
developments:
The 2011 law repealed and replaced the 1996 code and is the instrument behind the national population register ([code](2011-01-12-mauritanie-qanun-2011-003-mudawwanat-al-hala-al-madaniya-sijil-watani-lilsukkan)); law n. 2025-011 of 24 February 2025 repeals and replaces certain of its provisions ([amendment](2025-02-24-mauritanie-loi-2025-011-modifiant-code-etat-civil-actes-numeriques)).

Both texts are held in Arabic and the base does not hold a consolidated version, so which provisions the 2025 law changed is not established from the record.

summary: [Decree 2022-009](2022-01-01-primature-decret-2022-009-echanges-electroniques-autorites-administratives) governs electronic exchanges between users and administrations and between administrations, under the electronic transactions law of 2018.
developments:
The decree was made on the digital ministry's report under law n. 2018-022 of 12 June 2018 on electronic transactions, and is the legal footing the service portals rest on ([decree](2022-01-01-primature-decret-2022-009-echanges-electroniques-autorites-administratives)).

No implementing arrangement, register of compliant administrations or evaluation is held,; the national data management system it would serve is still in development, and the base holds no register of administrations exchanging under it.

summary: A [bill on access to and use of public information](2026-06-23-rsf-mauritanie-projet-loi-acces-utilisation-information-publique) is on the record from June 2026, presented as making good a presidential commitment.
developments:
A press-freedom organisation welcomed the bill and asked for strengthened guarantees ([bill](2026-06-23-rsf-mauritanie-projet-loi-acces-utilisation-information-publique)).

Nothing from the government or parliament on it is on file: no text, tabling date or parliamentary step. An advocacy organisation's welcome is the whole of what the base holds, which is the position this row records.

summary: The [2017 data protection law](2017-07-22-mrt-loi-2017-020-protection-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-apd) is being issued under: [deliberations of 2025](2025-07-14-mauritanie-apd-deliberation-004-2025-transfert-donnees-etranger-liste-pays-adequats) set rules for transfers abroad and for foreign cloud services.
developments:
Deliberation 004/2025 sets the conditions and procedural rules for transferring personal data abroad with a list of countries treated as adequate ([transfers](2025-07-14-mauritanie-apd-deliberation-004-2025-transfert-donnees-etranger-liste-pays-adequats)), and the amended text of deliberation 005/2025, published 30 April 2026, requires prior authorisation for processing personal data through cloud services abroad and contractual guarantees covering return of the data on expiry and its permanent deletion by the provider ([cloud](2026-04-30-apd-mauritanie-deliberation-005-2025-modifiee-cloud-etranger)).

The authority meets monthly with minutes issued, working on the inspection framework and its sworn agents ([inspections](2025-11-19-mauritanie-apd-reunion-mensuelle-referentiel-controle-agents-assermentes)) and on hosting inside the country ([hosting](2026-06-30-apd-reunion-mensuelle-hebergement-donnees-an-etat-homologation-datacenter)), against a published [strategic plan for 2023-2026](2023-01-01-apd-plan-strategique-2023-2026-protection-donnees).

No budget, staffing, caseload or sanction figure is published, so activity is dated and capacity is not. The amended text does not state which articles changed from the original.

summary: The data protection authority [set the conditions and procedural rules for transferring personal data abroad](2025-07-14-mauritanie-apd-deliberation-004-2025-transfert-donnees-etranger-liste-pays-adequats), with a list of countries treated as adequate.
developments:
Deliberation 004/2025 is the instrument ([transfers](2025-07-14-mauritanie-apd-deliberation-004-2025-transfert-donnees-etranger-liste-pays-adequats)); a companion deliberation sets minimum conditions for using cloud services hosted abroad ([cloud](2025-07-30-apd-mudawala-005-2025-khadamat-sahabiya-cloud-kharij)), and both were taken up again at the authority's monthly meeting of April 2026 ([meeting](2026-04-29-mauritanie-apd-reunion-mensuelle-transferts-etranger-cloud-deliberations-2025-004-005)).

The adequate-country list itself is not published, and no authorisation, refusal or transfer volume under the regime is on the record.

summary: [Decree 2023-113](2023-10-15-mauritanie-decret-2023-113-conseil-national-normalisation-comite-accreditation-jo-1543) created a national standardisation council and an accreditation committee and set the terms for accrediting conformity assessment bodies.
developments:
The decree of 7 September 2023 creates the National Standardisation and Quality Promotion Council and the Mauritanian Accreditation Committee ([decree](2023-10-15-mauritanie-decret-2023-113-conseil-national-normalisation-comite-accreditation-jo-1543)).

No membership, meeting record, accredited body or published standard is held for either institution, so the instrument exists and nothing on the record shows it working.

summary: The national infrastructure company [operates more than 1,760 km of fibre on three axes](2025-12-16-ami-inauguration-siege-sndin-reseau-fibre-1760-km), and a [regional programme's backbone loan closed in 2022](2022-08-26-world-bank-warcip-apl2-icr-mauritanie-backbone-national).
developments:
The kilometre figure is the company's own, given at the inauguration of its headquarters in December 2025, with no route map, capacity, utilisation or wholesale tariff beside it ([network](2025-12-16-ami-inauguration-siege-sndin-reseau-fibre-1760-km)).

The regional communications infrastructure programme's second loan closed with an implementation completion report covering the national backbone it financed ([completion](2022-08-26-world-bank-warcip-apl2-icr-mauritanie-backbone-national)).

The relationship between the two - what the programme built and what the company now runs - is not established by anything on file.

summary: The base holds a [2014 feasibility study for a national exchange point](2014-06-16-mauritanie-warcip-rapport-faisabilite-point-echange-internet-ixp) and nothing since saying whether one was established.
developments:
The final study was completed under the regional connectivity project in June 2014, setting out the state of the internet sector and its market data ([study](2014-06-16-mauritanie-warcip-rapport-faisabilite-point-echange-internet-ixp)).

Twelve years on, nothing on the record says whether an exchange point exists. A published operator listing or peering record would settle it, and the row is carried as a dated absence rather than as a finding either way.

summary: The [Nouakchott data centre](2025-05-08-ami-inauguration-data-center-nouakchott-1372m2-100-baies) runs to 1,372 m2 and 100 server racks, and the [national cloud was inaugurated on it](2026-06-29-ami-tadshin-sahaba-wataniya-mauritanie-cloud-national) in June 2026.
developments:
The facility was inaugurated by the President on 8 May 2025 as the first national installation of its kind, presented as certified to international standards and stated as extensible ([inauguration](2025-05-08-ami-inauguration-data-center-nouakchott-1372m2-100-baies)).

The national cloud was inaugurated at it on 29 June 2026, the minister telling parliament three days later that its launch removes the need to host state services internationally ([cloud](2026-06-29-ami-tadshin-sahaba-wataniya-mauritanie-cloud-national), [statement](2026-07-02-ami-ministre-lancement-cloud-national-assemblee-nationale)).

The certification is asserted rather than evidenced, no tier rating or operator is named, and utilisation, customers and load are unpublished. A backup data centre was specified under the earlier connectivity programme and nothing says whether it was built ([specification](2021-02-09-mtnima-warcip-dao-station-specifications-datacenter-secours)).

summary: Two framework agreements of June 2026 [fund 85 rural mini-grids](2026-06-19-islamic-development-bank-mrt-2026-02-rural-electrification), and the [National Assembly passed the financing bills](2026-07-31-ami-assemblee-nationale-ratification-financements-bid-electrification-rurale) in July.
developments:
The agreements were signed on 19 June 2026 and the bills authorising the financing passed on 31 July 2026 ([financing](2026-06-19-islamic-development-bank-mrt-2026-02-rural-electrification), [ratification](2026-07-31-ami-assemblee-nationale-ratification-financements-bid-electrification-rurale)).

A national energy compact issued under the continental access initiative sets the country's commitments on electricity access ([compact](2024-12-01-mauritanie-pacte-national-energie-mission-300)).

No amount, site list, connection target or delivery date is held for the mini-grids, and nothing states whether any of them serve telecommunications sites - which is what would connect this to the network's own power problem.

summary: The central bank [regulates payment institutions and their agents](2022-03-31-bcm-instruction-03-gr-2022-reglementation-etablissements-de-paiement) under 2022 instructions and carries a [digital payment strategy for 2023-2028](2024-09-12-bcm-strategie-nationale-paiement-numerique-2023-2028).
developments:
Instruction 03/GR/2022 regulates payment institutions and instruction 05/GR/2022 regulates the agents of payment service providers and the protection of their customers, both issued on 31 March 2022 ([institutions](2022-03-31-bcm-instruction-03-gr-2022-reglementation-etablissements-de-paiement), [agents](2022-03-31-bcm-instruction-05-gr-2022-agents-prestataires-services-paiement-protection-consommateurs)).

The bank's digital payment strategy for 2023-2028 sets five objectives, among them easing the regulation of payment and electronic money institutions to attract fintech investment and building an instant-payment system ([strategy](2024-09-12-bcm-strategie-nationale-paiement-numerique-2023-2028)); it is presented as an extension of the [financial inclusion strategy](2023-01-01-bcm-strategie-nationale-inclusion-financiere-snif-2023-2028).

The payment, clearing and securities settlement systems council met in May and July 2026, welcoming progress in modernising the financial system ([council](2026-07-13-bcm-conseil-systemes-paiement-compensation-reglement-titres), [progress](2026-05-19-saharamedias-bcm-conseil-systemes-paiement-modernisation-systeme-financier)). No register of licensed institutions, agent count or supervisory action is published, and no implementation report against the strategy is on file.

summary: A [verification platform opened for a social transfer covering more than 2 million registered citizens](2026-06-01-mrt-taazour-plateforme-aoun-verification-2057006-citoyens), its cash component run through the interbank payment operator.
developments:
The AOUN transfer covers more than 2,057,006 citizens recorded in the social register, and its cash-transfer component is run by the solidarity delegation with the national deposit and development fund and the interbank payment operator ([platform](2026-06-01-mrt-taazour-plateforme-aoun-verification-2057006-citoyens), [transfers](2026-06-12-ami-aoun-transferts-numeriques-taazour-cndd-gimtel)).

An electronic payment platform was delivered under the first safety-net project ([completion](2021-04-15-worldbank-icr-mauritania-social-safety-net-plateforme-paiement-electronique)).

The figure is the number registered rather than the number paid, and no payment completion rate, exclusion-error estimate or grievance route is published.

summary: The [national register holds more than 5.1 million people](2026-06-18-mrt-registre-national-population-5-1-millions-parlement) and enrolment is described as a permanent public service; the [civil status code was amended in 2025](2025-02-24-mauritanie-loi-2025-011-modifiant-code-etat-civil-actes-numeriques).
developments:
The interior minister gave the figure to parliament on 18 June 2026 and separately described enrolment as having become a permanent public service guaranteeing every citizen's right to be registered ([figure](2026-06-18-mrt-registre-national-population-5-1-millions-parlement), [enrolment](2026-06-18-ami-kassataya-enrolement-registre-national-population-service-public-permanent)).

The system for running the register and secure documents was renewed in August 2021 across 153 reception centres ([system](2021-08-03-ami-anrpts-nizam-mundamij-sijil-sukkan-153-markaz-istiqbal)), and the ministry's own half-year report for 2026 records the biometric interconnection of the register with civil status ([interconnection](2026-06-01-dgat-interieur-bilan-premier-semestre-2026-interconnexion-biometrique-etat-civil)).

No denominator, coverage rate or age breakdown accompanies the 5.1 million, and no independent audit of the register is held.

summary: [Terms of reference were issued in March 2025](2025-03-10-mrt-mtnima-wardip-tdr-systeme-adressage-geolocalise-mauripost) for a geolocated addressing system to be implemented through the postal company, and nothing has followed on the record.
developments:
The terms of reference were issued under the regional digital integration programme, presenting the system as favouring the development of commerce and electronic commerce in particular ([terms](2025-03-10-mrt-mtnima-wardip-tdr-systeme-adressage-geolocalise-mauripost)).

Eighteen months on, no award, supplier, coverage, address standard or delivery date is on the record, so what exists is a specification and not a register.

summary: [Law 2021-005](2021-02-10-mrt-loi-2021-005-registre-commerce-suretes-mobilieres) amends the Commercial Code and carries the trade register and the movable securities regime; nothing states whether either runs electronically.
developments:
The law of 10 February 2021 amends, completes and repeals provisions of the Commercial Code of 2000 ([law](2021-02-10-mrt-loi-2021-005-registre-commerce-suretes-mobilieres)).

An investment code of February 2025 and its application decree of August 2025 carry a single-window arrangement for investors ([code](2025-02-19-mauritanie-code-des-investissements-loi-2025-006-apim), [decree](2025-08-14-mrt-decret-2025-117-application-code-investissements-guichet-unique)), and no operating single window, service list, processing time or investor count is on the record.

Nothing says how many entries either register holds.

summary: The [social register carries more than 2 million citizens](2026-06-01-mrt-taazour-plateforme-aoun-verification-2057006-citoyens), and a [separate database for disaster-affected households](2025-10-15-mrt-decret-2025-162-bds-mac-base-donnees-menages-catastrophes) was created by decree in October 2025.
developments:
The delegation ran a coordination round to update the register across the Nouakchott wilayas in April 2026 ([update](2026-04-30-ami-taazour-acces-plateforme-registre-social-wilayas-nouakchott)), and the safety-net programme behind it was re-established by decree in May 2024 ([decree](2024-05-15-mrt-decret-2024-073-creation-programme-tekavoul-registre-social)).

Decree n. 2025-162 creates a special database for poor and vulnerable households affected by disasters ([disaster database](2025-10-15-mrt-decret-2025-162-bds-mac-base-donnees-menages-catastrophes)); no operator, household count or relationship to the social register is stated for it.

progress: No change, a single count with no earlier figure behind it
summary: [1,939,343 registered voters](2024-07-03-mrt-conseil-constitutionnel-deliberation-2024-004-inscrits-1939343) on the Constitutional Council's proclamation of the 2024 presidential result.
developments:
The figure is the roll as it stood at the 2024 presidential election, taken from the Council's own deliberation proclaiming the definitive results ([proclamation](2024-07-03-mrt-conseil-constitutionnel-deliberation-2024-004-inscrits-1939343)).

No later revision, audit or statement of the register's relationship to the national population register is on the record, so the base holds one dated count and no series.

summary: The [tax procedures book](2019-10-07-mrt-dgi-livre-procedures-fiscales-dispositions-communes-nif) carries the tax identification number and the obligations attaching to it.
developments:
The common provisions of the procedures book are what the base holds on the identifier ([provisions](2019-10-07-mrt-dgi-livre-procedures-fiscales-dispositions-communes-nif)).

No registered-taxpayer count, coverage figure or link to the business or population registers is published, so the identifier exists in law and its reach is unmeasured.

summary: An [electronic consultation register is producing usable epidemic-response data in two wilayas](2026-07-17-oms-afro-registre-consultation-electronique-hodh-chargui-gharbi), and a [national digital health project selected its pilot sites](2026-04-30-mauritanie-digisante-mr-selection-sites-pilote) in April 2026.
developments:
The health organisation's account puts the register as giving reliable data for epidemic response in Hodh El Chargui and Hodh El Gharbi ([register](2026-07-17-oms-afro-registre-consultation-electronique-hodh-chargui-gharbi)).

The health minister said in January 2026 that work was under way to generalise the model reference hospitals' information systems ([hospitals](2026-01-28-mrt-ministre-sante-assemblee-systemes-information-sanitaire-hopitaux)), the ministry discussed digitising the system with the lender in March ([lender](2026-03-09-mrt-ministere-sante-banque-mondiale-plateforme-numerique-donnees-sante)), and an order of December 2021 fixes the regional health system's data collection ([order](2021-12-14-mrt-arrete-1496-systeme-regional-sante-snis-collecte-donnees)).

No facility count, completeness rate, reporting timeliness figure or national rollout date is published.

summary: The [customs system is reached over the internet](2023-02-01-mrt-douanes-guide-utilisateur-sydonia-world-via-internet) under a published user guide, and its reforms are [carried in the monetary fund's fifth review](2026-02-05-mrt-imf-country-report-26-027-dgi-douanes-zone-franche-jibaya).
developments:
The finance ministry published the user guide for connecting to the system over the internet in February 2023 ([guide](2023-02-01-mrt-douanes-guide-utilisateur-sydonia-world-via-internet)).

The fund's fifth programme review of February 2026 carries the customs and tax administration reforms running on it alongside the free-zone arrangements ([review](2026-02-05-mrt-imf-country-report-26-027-dgi-douanes-zone-franche-jibaya)).

No declaration volume, clearance time or coverage figure is published, and a programme review is not an evaluation of the system.

summary: [39 per cent of large enterprises file tax online](2026-03-13-mrt-worldbank-isr-p179263-taxes-en-ligne-grandes-entreprises-39pc) on the financier's project indicator, against a revenue strategy carrying remote declaration.
developments:
The figure is a project indicator reported by the lender in March 2026, with no denominator, target or comparison for other taxpayer segments beside it ([indicator](2026-03-13-mrt-worldbank-isr-p179263-taxes-en-ligne-grandes-entreprises-39pc)).

The revenue directorate's strategic plan for 2025-2029 carries remote declaration among its objectives ([plan](2025-03-01-mrt-dgi-plan-strategique-2025-2029-jibaya-teledeclaration)), and a workshop in July 2026 took up electronic invoicing for public entities and remote payment ([workshop](2026-07-30-ami-dgi-facturation-electronique-entites-publiques-telepaiement)).

summary: A [cadastral referential and unique parcel identifier](2026-08-27-mauritanie-conseil-ministres-referentiel-cadastral-identifiant-parcellaire-casier-judiciaire) went before the Council of Ministers in August 2026, after a [digital census of built parcels in Nouakchott](2026-05-12-mrt-recensement-numerique-parcelles-baties-nouakchott-identifiant-unique).
developments:
The property ministry launched the digitisation of the land sector in January 2026 ([launch](2026-01-23-mrt-ministere-domaines-leegou-aqaar-el-mouhafid-numerisation-fonciere)) and opened the parcel census carrying a unique identifier in May ([census](2026-05-12-mrt-recensement-numerique-parcelles-baties-nouakchott-identifiant-unique)); a workshop on a land data warehouse ran under a land project the same month ([warehouse](2026-05-04-mrt-atelier-foncier-projet-aakar-entrepot-donnees-foncieres-basira)).

A Council decree of September 2025 provides for electronic land transactions and their interoperability ([decree](2025-09-02-mauritanie-conseil-ministres-decret-transactions-foncieres-electroniques-interoperabilite)).

No parcel count, coverage figure, completion date or link to the population register is published.

summary: An [annual bulletin on communal finances](2026-07-01-tresor-dfl-note-conjoncture-finances-locales-2025-sigel) is produced from the local financial management system, and [digital counters](2026-02-24-agence-ecofin-guichet-numerique-bassikounou-fracture-numerique) are opening in remote towns.
developments:
The Treasury's local finance directorate publishes the bulletin from the local financial management system ([bulletin](2026-07-01-tresor-dfl-note-conjoncture-finances-locales-2025-sigel)), and a ministry report sets out what the communes can and cannot run institutionally ([capacity](2022-11-01-dgct-midec-rapport-capacites-institutionnelles-communes-mdp)).

A digital counter opened at Bassikounou to bring public services closer to citizens ([counter](2026-02-24-agence-ecofin-guichet-numerique-bassikounou-fracture-numerique)) and a digital space at Ouadane ([space](2025-12-21-ami-ouverture-espace-numerique-ouadane-adrar-giz)).

No commune runs a digital service of its own on the record: the counters are the central ministry's and the finance system is the Treasury's.

summary: The [competition for 3,000 state officials was run end to end through the services portal](2026-07-09-ami-concours-3000-agents-etat-ia-preparation-correction-khidmaty), with artificial intelligence used in preparing and marking it.
developments:
The digital minister said in February 2026 that the whole recruitment process would be digitised ([direction](2026-02-25-mauritanie-conseil-ministres-decret-concours-numeriques-ia-recrutement-3000-agents)), and candidates interviewed after sitting it praised the transparency of the process ([competition](2026-07-09-ami-concours-3000-agents-etat-ia-preparation-correction-khidmaty)).

How artificial intelligence was used in marking is not set out, no error, appeal or audit arrangement is published, and the candidate reaction is reported rather than surveyed - so what is established is that the tool was used and not how well.

summary: An [artificial-intelligence agrometeorological early warning system](2026-01-14-ami-onm-pnud-systeme-alerte-precoce-agrometeorologique-ia-rosso) was worked through at Rosso in January 2026 with a UN development agency.
developments:
The workshop was run by the meteorological office with the development agency ([workshop](2026-01-14-ami-onm-pnud-systeme-alerte-precoce-agrometeorologique-ia-rosso)); a separate hydrometeorological early warning system for the Senegal River valley is described by its developer as artificial-intelligence powered ([system](2026-01-01-paneotech-hydromet-ai-systeme-alerte-precoce-vallee-fleuve-senegal)).

Neither account states what the models do, what data they use, who receives the warnings or whether either system is in operation.

summary: Two open repositories carry [language data for the country's languages](2026-05-16-github-mwiml-open-data-mauritania-nlp-langues-nationales), and the [draft national strategy](2024-04-01-mauritania-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy-2024-2029-draft) runs on five priorities and thirty measures.
developments:
A Hassaniya dialect dataset collection was published on a model-hosting platform in January 2026 ([datasets](2026-01-20-huggingface-ai-for-rim-hassaniya-dialect-datasets-llm)) and an open natural-language hub for Pulaar, Soninke and Hassaniya on a code-hosting platform in May ([hub](2026-05-16-github-mwiml-open-data-mauritania-nlp-langues-nationales)); both are community repositories rather than state assets and neither is named in the strategy.

The draft strategy covers skills, research, international collaboration, data governance and ethical use, with sector projects in health, education, agriculture, fisheries, transport, energy and defence ([strategy](2024-04-01-mauritania-national-artificial-intelligence-strategy-2024-2029-draft)). The base holds a draft and no adoption instrument.

summary: A [European-supported programme ran a session with the audiovisual regulator on deepfakes and synthetic media](2026-07-02-eces-lead-ai-nouakchott-hapa-deepfakes-medias-synthetiques) in July 2026.
developments:
The session was held in Nouakchott with the audiovisual regulator ([programme](2026-07-02-eces-lead-ai-nouakchott-hapa-deepfakes-medias-synthetiques)).

No regulatory instrument, guideline or enforcement power on synthetic media follows from it on the record, and the account is the implementing organisation's own. Awareness work is what the base holds and a rule is not.

summary: A [technology incubator at Nouakchott](2022-01-01-hadina-rimtic-incubateur-technologique-nouakchott-impact) supports startups and small firms, and a [one-day artificial-intelligence build](2026-05-17-nouakchott-ai-build-premier-hackathon-ia-25-equipes) was held in May 2026.
developments:
The incubator presents itself as building an entrepreneurial base with economic, social and sustainable impact, accompanying startups and small and medium enterprises to growth ([incubator](2022-01-01-hadina-rimtic-incubateur-technologique-nouakchott-impact)).

The build was held on 17 May 2026 to launch working projects in the country ([build](2026-05-17-nouakchott-ai-build-premier-hackathon-ia-25-equipes)).

Both records are the organisers' own sites: no cohort count, funding, survival rate, project outcome or public support is established from either.

summary: A [national platform for training public servants in essential digital skills](2024-06-10-mtnima-plateforme-nationale-temekoun-competences-numeriques-fonction-publique) was presented in June 2024, and [300 officials entered a cybersecurity programme](2025-12-15-ami-programme-formation-cybersecurite-ia-300-fonctionnaires) in December 2025.
developments:
The platform was presented at a ministry workshop ([platform](2024-06-10-mtnima-plateforme-nationale-temekoun-competences-numeriques-fonction-publique)), and nothing on the record since says whether it is in use: no enrolment, completion or curriculum figure is published.

The cybersecurity programme was launched for 300 state officials ([programme](2025-12-15-ami-programme-formation-cybersecurite-ia-300-fonctionnaires)) with no curriculum, duration, provider or completion figure beside it.

A study for a national continuing training policy reached a restitution workshop in May 2026 ([policy](2026-05-07-fonction-publique-atelier-restitution-politique-nationale-formation-continue)).

summary: The [complaints platform handled 97 per cent of what it received in its first twelve months](2025-11-19-ami-bilan-plateforme-ain-12-mois-97-pourcent-traites), on the minister's own account.
developments:
The platform was launched by the Prime Minister on 22 October 2024 to receive and handle citizens' complaints ([launch](2024-10-22-ami-lancement-plateforme-ain-plaintes-citoyens)), and the digital minister gave the twelve-month figure at the government spokesman's briefing ([result](2025-11-19-ami-bilan-plateforme-ain-12-mois-97-pourcent-traites)).

Handled is the minister's own word, and [no volume, category breakdown, resolution time or outcome is published beside the 97 per cent](2025-11-19-ami-bilan-plateforme-ain-12-mois-97-pourcent-traites), so what it counts is not established.

summary: Technical assistance for a [citizen participation platform was provisionally awarded](2026-05-07-mtnima-wardip-attribution-provisoire-plateforme-participation-citoyenne) in May 2026, against an [e-participation policy still held as a 2023 draft](2023-12-01-mtnima-politique-nationale-participation-electronique).
developments:
The draft policy was proposed by a UN regional commission in December 2023, benchmarked against Tunisia, Morocco and Denmark and carrying a vision, strategic objectives and an assessment of the country's e-participation ([policy](2023-12-01-mtnima-politique-nationale-participation-electronique)).

The assistance was provisionally awarded under the regional digital integration programme ([award](2026-05-07-mtnima-wardip-attribution-provisoire-plateforme-participation-citoyenne)).

A provisional award is not a contract: no supplier, value, scope or delivery date is published, and the policy carries no adoption instrument.

summary: The [2006 ordinance on the promotion and protection of persons with disabilities](2006-11-23-mauritanie-ordonnance-2006-043-promotion-protection-personnes-handicapees) is the frame, and its [implementing decrees are outstanding](2026-07-01-cndh-observations-epu-mauritanie-decrets-application-loi-handicap).
developments:
The national human rights commission's observations on the periodic review in July 2026 record that implementing decrees for the disability law have not been made ([observations](2026-07-01-cndh-observations-epu-mauritanie-decrets-application-loi-handicap)).

Transfers were made to 6,000 children with special needs around the international day in December 2025 ([transfers](2025-12-04-ami-journee-internationale-personnes-handicapees-transferts-6000-enfants)).

Nothing on the record addresses digital accessibility of public services for disabled users, which is the question this indicator asks.

summary: [Decree 2022-063](2022-05-15-mauritanie-decret-2022-063-refugies-personnes-a-proteger-jo-1509) replaced the 2005 refugee decree, and refugee registration in the eastern region is [reported alongside inscription in the national register](2026-01-01-unhcr-hodh-chargui-factsheet-mauritanie-2025-overview-registre-national).
developments:
The decree of 5 May 2022 fixes how the international refugee conventions apply in Mauritania ([decree](2022-05-15-mauritanie-decret-2022-063-refugies-personnes-a-proteger-jo-1509)), and the refugee agency's 2025 overview for Hodh Chargui reports registration there ([factsheet](2026-01-01-unhcr-hodh-chargui-factsheet-mauritanie-2025-overview-registre-national)).

No registered-refugee count, card issuance figure or statement of what the national register records for refugees is carried in either, so inclusion is provided for in law and unmeasured in practice.

summary: The [decadal statistics strategy runs to 2030](2021-01-01-mauritanie-snds-strategie-nationale-decennale-developpement-statistique-2021-2030) but its first action plan covered 2021-2025 and no successor plan or implementation report is held.
developments:
The strategy carries an action plan for 2021-2025 whose period has run out ([strategy](2021-01-01-mauritanie-snds-strategie-nationale-decennale-developpement-statistique-2021-2030)).

The statistics agency's orientation council was named in Council of Ministers in March 2026 ([council](2026-03-04-mauritanie-conseil-ministres-projet-loi-archives-nationales-nomination-conseil-orientation-ansade)), and the agency publishes monthly statistical bulletins carrying a communications price index ([bulletin](2026-01-12-ansade-bulletin-decembre-2025-indice-prix-communication)).

The country's position on the continental statistics charter is recorded on the union's own list ([charter](2023-09-19-african-union-african-charter-on-statistics-signature-ratification-status-list)).

summary: The continental body [installed new climate services and satellite reception infrastructure](2025-09-23-auc-climsa-puma-nouakchott-satellite-reception-inspection) for the national meteorological services, inspected in September 2025.
developments:
The meteorological office runs to a strategic plan for 2024-2030 ([plan](2023-06-01-onm-mauritanie-plan-strategique-national-2024-2030-meteorologie)), and a continental earth-observation programme held its fourth national workshop on using earth observation for natural resource management in July 2025 ([workshop](2025-07-29-oss-gmes-africa-mauritanie-cuct-services-observation-terre)).

No station count, data product, availability figure or user of the outputs is published, and the strategic plan's implementation is not reported.

summary: The one instrument on file is a [clean energy cooperation memorandum between the two energy ministries](2023-12-03-doe-mpme-mauritanie-mou-clean-energy-cooperation), signed in December 2023.
developments:
The memorandum text is held ([memorandum](2023-12-03-doe-mpme-mauritanie-mou-clean-energy-cooperation)).

No value, work programme, duration or activity under it is on the record since, and the base holds no engagement with a United States technology company at all - which is the substance this indicator asks about.

progress: No change, a statute in force since 2021 that the base has only now acquired
summary: [Law 2021-014 on electronic payment services and means](2021-07-30-mtnima-loi-2021-014-services-moyens-paiement-electronique) has been in force since July 2021 and is the statute the central bank's payment instructions are issued under.
developments:
The Official Gazette text of 30 July 2021 covers definitions, electronic payment services and means, payment cards and the contestation of a card payment ([law](2021-07-30-mtnima-loi-2021-014-services-moyens-paiement-electronique), [text](2021-07-30-mauritanie-loi-2021-014-texte-integral-droit-afrique)).

The held capture is an excerpt cut off partway through Titre III, so the later articles the central bank's own instruction cites are not on file, and no implementing decree, licensing decision or amendment to the statute is held.

summary: Using cloud services hosted abroad for personal data [requires prior authorisation from the data protection authority](2026-04-30-apd-mauritanie-deliberation-005-2025-modifiee-cloud-etranger) under the amended deliberation of April 2026.
developments:
The amended text of deliberation 005/2025, published 30 April 2026, requires public and private bodies using cloud services abroad to obtain prior authorisation for the processing, a separate transfer authorisation where the host country is not on the approved list, and contractual guarantees covering compliance with the 2017 law, a data-transfer clause, return of the data on contract expiry and its permanent deletion by the provider ([deliberation](2026-04-30-apd-mauritanie-deliberation-005-2025-modifiee-cloud-etranger)).

The authority has also taken up homologation of the national data centre at its monthly meeting ([hosting](2026-06-30-apd-reunion-mensuelle-hebergement-donnees-an-etat-homologation-datacenter)). No general localisation requirement, sector rule or list of authorisations granted is held, and the approved-country list the regime turns on is not published.
